sop: SOP-QA-008 Production procedures, deviations and reprocessing (synthetic)

ranking.title: 211.86 Use of approved components, drug product containers, and closures.

rows.text: There shall be written procedures for production and process control designed to assure that the drug products have the identity, strength, quality, and purity they purport or are represented to possess.

passages.text:
1. Purpose

To set out how production and process control procedures are written, approved and followed, how departures from them are handled, and when a batch may be reprocessed.

3. Production procedures

3.1 Every production and process control step is described in a written procedure. Together, the production SOPs listed in Annex 1 cover every requirement of 21 CFR 211 Subpart F. 3.2 Each production SOP is written by Production, reviewed by Engineering where equipment is involved, and approved by QA. Changes follow the same route. 3.3 Operators follow the procedures and complete the batch record at the end of each shift.

4. Deviations

Any departure from a written procedure is recorded on a deviation form with its reason and QA's assessment.

rows.text: Written procedures shall be established and followed prescribing a system for reprocessing batches that do not conform to standards or specifications and the steps to be taken to insure that the reprocessed batches will conform with all established standards, specifications, and characteristics.

5. Reprocessing

5.1 A batch that fails a specification may be reprocessed only under a written reprocessing protocol that states the steps to be taken and the tests the reprocessed batch must pass. 5.2 The production manager approves each reprocessing protocol.
